title: Etaleness of a finitely presented algebra map descends along a directed colimit of base rings
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $A_i\to A_{i'}$ for $i\le i'$, compatible), with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $0\in I$, let $B_0$ and $C_0$ be commutative $A_0$-algebras and $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras which is of finite presentation ($C_0\cong B_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ as $B_0$-algebras for some $n,m\ge0$). For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via the transition map, and $A$ via the coprojection, and put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi_i=\mathrm{id}_{A_i}\otimes\varphi_0:B_i\to C_i$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\varphi_0:B\to C$. If the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ induced by $\varphi$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], then there is an $i\ge0$ such that the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ induced by $\varphi_i$ is etale (Stacks Algebra, Lemma 07RI).

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RI (lemma-colimit-etale, line 47626) and its proof (presentation $C_0=B_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_{1,0},\dots,f_{m,0})$, the isomorphism $\mathrm d:(f)/(f)^2\to\bigoplus C\,\mathrm dx_k$ lifted to a finite stage); etale ring maps in the sense of $\operatorname{Spec}$ of [def-weil-etale-morphism], as in lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change

proof.text:
*Step 1 (presentations at every stage).* Write $P_0=B_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $C_0\cong P_0/J_0$ with $J_0=(f_{1,0},\dots,f_{m,0})$ (hypothesis), and let $T$ be either $A_i$ for some $i\ge0$ or $A$, an $A_0$-algebra as in the statement; put $B_T=T\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $P_T=T\otimes_{A_0}P_0$, $C_T=T\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ (so $B_T=B_i,C_T=C_i$ resp. $B,C$). (a) $P_T\cong B_T[x_1,\dots,x_n]$: by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=A_0$, $S=B_0$, the $R$-algebra $T$ and the $S$-algebra $P_0$) and symmetry of $\otimes$, $T\otimes_{A_0}P_0\cong B_T\otimes_{B_0}P_0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=B_0$, $R=B_T$) $B_T\otimes_{B_0}B_0[x]\cong B_T[x]$; the composite sends $t\otimes\sum_
u b_
u x^
u\mapsto\sum_
u(t\otimes b_
u)x^
u$, i.e. it is the coefficient map $B_0	o B_T$ on $P_0$, and it is $B_T$-linear. (b) $C_T\cong B_T[x]/J_T$, $J_T=(f_{1,T},\dots,f_{m,T})$ with $f_{j,T}$ the image of $f_{j,0}$ under the coefficient map: by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=A_0$, $S=P_0$, the $R$-algebra $T$ and the $S$-algebra $C_0$) $T\otimes_{A_0}C_0\cong(P_0/J_0)\otimes_{P_0}P_T$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=P_0$, $B=P_T$, $I=J_0$) this is $P_T/J_0P_T=P_T/(f_{1,T},\dots,f_{m,T})$, compatibly with the maps from $B_T$ (so the induced $B_T$-algebra structure is the one through $\varphi_T=\mathrm{id}_T\otimes\varphi_0$). (c) For $0\le i\le i'$ the maps $P_i	o P_{i'}$ and $P_i	o P_A$ induced by $A_i	o A_{i'}$, $A_i	o A$ (tensored with $P_0$) become, under (a), application of the ring maps $B_i	o B_{i'}$, $B_i	o B$ to the coefficients (check on $t\otimes bx^
u$); hence they are ring maps sending $x_k\mapsto x_k$ and $f_{j,i}\mapsto f_{j,i'}$ resp. $f_{j,A}$, and they commute with the formal partial derivatives $\partial/\partial x_l$ (a coefficientwise ring map does, by the formula $\partial x^
u/\partial x_l=
u_lx^{
u-e_l}$). (Stacks: 'Note that $C_i=B_i[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,i},\ldots,f_{m,i})$ ... Note that $C=B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$'.)

*Step 2 (etaleness as the conormal map).* For each $T$ of step 1, $J_T$ is the kernel of the surjection $B_T[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to C_T$ and is generated by $f_{1,T},\dots,f_{m,T}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-conormal-criterion] (with $R=B_T$, $S=C_T$) applies: writing $\mathrm d_T:J_T/J_T^2\to\bigoplus_kC_T\,\mathrm dx_k$, $\mathrm d_T(g)=\sum_k(\partial g/\partial x_k\bmod J_T)\,\mathrm dx_k$, the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_T\to\operatorname{Spec}B_T$ induced by $\varphi_T$ is etale iff $\mathrm d_T$ is bijective. By hypothesis ($T=A$), $\mathrm d_A$ is bijective; it suffices to find $i\ge0$ with $\mathrm d_{A_i}$ bijective. Write $f_j=f_{j,A}$, $P=P_A=B[x]$, $J=J_A$. (Stacks: 'The assumption is that the map $\mathrm d:(f_1,\ldots,f_m)/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)^2\to\bigoplus C\,\mathrm dx_k$ is an isomorphism'.)

*Step 3 (finitely many identities over $A$).* As $\mathrm d_A$ is surjective, for each $k=1,\dots,n$ there is $\xi_k\in J/J^2$ with $\mathrm d_A\xi_k=\mathrm dx_k$; write $\xi_k$ as the class of $\sum_jc_{jk}f_j$ with $c_{jk}\in P$. By the Leibniz rule $\partial(c f_j)/\partial x_l=c\,\partial f_j/\partial x_l+f_j\,\partial c/\partial x_l\equiv c\,\partial f_j/\partial x_l\pmod J$, so $\mathrm d_A\xi_k=\sum_l(\sum_jc_{jk}\partial f_j/\partial x_l\bmod J)\,\mathrm dx_l$, and $\mathrm d_A\xi_k=\mathrm dx_k$ says, comparing coefficients in the free module, (a) $\sum_jc_{jk}\,\partial f_j/\partial x_l-\delta_{kl}\in J$ for all $k,l$. Next, for each $j$ the element $\eta_j=\sum_k(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)\xi_k-\bar f_j\in J/J^2$ ($\bar f_j$ the class of $f_j$) satisfies $\mathrm d_A\eta_j=\sum_k(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)\mathrm dx_k-\mathrm d_A\bar f_j=0$ ($\mathrm d_A$ is $C$-linear); as $\mathrm d_A$ is injective, $\eta_j=0$, i.e. (b) $\sum_k(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)\sum_{j'}c_{j'k}f_{j'}-f_j\in J^2$ for all $j$. Writing out the memberships, there are $e_{kl\,j'}\in P$ and $h_{j\,j'j''}\in P$ with (a') $\sum_jc_{jk}\,\partial f_j/\partial x_l-\delta_{kl}=\sum_{j'}e_{klj'}f_{j'}$ and (b') $\sum_k(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)\sum_{j'}c_{j'k}f_{j'}-f_j=\sum_{j',j''}h_{jj'j''}f_{j'}f_{j''}$: finitely many polynomial identities in $P$ (as $J^2$ is generated by the products $f_{j'}f_{j''}$).

*Step 4 (descending the identities to a stage).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] with $M_0=P_0$ (an $A_0$-module), so $M_i=P_i$, $M=P$. By its part (1), each of the finitely many elements $c_{jk},e_{klj'},h_{jj'j''}$ of $P$ is the image of an element of some $P_{i_\bullet}$; $I$ being directed, take $i\ge0$ above all these indices and replace the preimages by their images in $P_i$ (compatibility of the maps $\mu$): we get $c'_{jk},e'_{klj'},h'_{jj'j''}\in P_i$ mapping to $c_{jk},e_{klj'},h_{jj'j''}$. Consider the finitely many elements $u_{kl}=\sum_jc'_{jk}\partial f_{j,i}/\partial x_l-\delta_{kl}-\sum_{j'}e'_{klj'}f_{j',i}$ and $v_j=\sum_k(\partial f_{j,i}/\partial x_k)\sum_{j'}c'_{j'k}f_{j',i}-f_{j,i}-\sum_{j',j''}h'_{jj'j''}f_{j',i}f_{j'',i}$ of $P_i$. By step 1 (c) the map $P_i\to P$ is a ring map sending $f_{j,i}\mapsto f_j$ and commuting with $\partial/\partial x_l$, so it sends $u_{kl}$, $v_j$ to the left minus right sides of (a'), (b'), which are $0$. By part (2) each $u_{kl}$, $v_j$ is killed by $P_i\to P_{i'}$ for some $i'\ge i$; take one $i'$ above these finitely many indices and replace $i$ by $i'$ and $c',e',h'$ by their images (step 1 (c) again). Then $u_{kl}=0$ and $v_j=0$ in $P_i$ for all $k,l,j$. (Stacks: 'Thus for sufficiently large $i$ we can find elements $\xi_{k,i}$ ... Moreover, on increasing $i$ if necessary ... since this is true in the limit'.)

*Step 5 ($\mathrm d_{A_i}$ is bijective; conclusion).* Work at the index $i$ of step 4, $J_i=J_{A_i}$, $\mathrm d_i=\mathrm d_{A_i}$. Put $\xi_{k,i}=$ class of $\sum_jc'_{jk}f_{j,i}$ in $J_i/J_i^2$ and let $s:\bigoplus_kC_i\,\mathrm dx_k\to J_i/J_i^2$ be the $C_i$-linear map with $s(\mathrm dx_k)=\xi_{k,i}$. By the Leibniz computation of step 3 and $u_{kl}=0$, $\mathrm d_i\xi_{k,i}=\sum_l(\sum_jc'_{jk}\partial f_{j,i}/\partial x_l\bmod J_i)\mathrm dx_l=\sum_l\delta_{kl}\mathrm dx_l=\mathrm dx_k$, so $\mathrm d_i\circ s=\mathrm{id}$ on the basis, hence everywhere. By $v_j=0$, $s(\mathrm d_i\bar f_{j,i})=\sum_k(\partial f_{j,i}/\partial x_k\bmod J_i)\xi_{k,i}=\bar f_{j,i}$ in $J_i/J_i^2$ (the term with $h'$ lies in $J_i^2$). Since $J_i$ is generated by the $f_{j,i}$, $J_i/J_i^2$ is generated as a $C_i$-module by the classes $\bar f_{j,i}$, and $s\circ\mathrm d_i$ is $C_i$-linear, so $s\circ\mathrm d_i=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\mathrm d_i$ is bijective with inverse $s$, and by step 2 ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-conormal-criterion] with $R=B_i$, $S=C_i$) the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ induced by $\varphi_i$ is etale. (Stacks: 'Then this $i$ works.')
